entry_state: Equity awards retain grant-date measurement while service estimates change; cash awards remeasure liabilities. Settlement choice, cancellation and beneficial modification have separate rules, with original and incremental service costs retained. Participation allocates earnings before EPS, and assumed settlement can alter its numerator. The next example introduces a senior entitlement and cap whose allocation continues next.
exit_state: The capped-participation allocation recalculates class earnings after assumed issuance and supports ordering only for complete additive gross effects. A shared bonus and tax schedule makes conversion effects nonadditive, so correct hypothetical worlds do not themselves settle admissible dilution selection. A contingent-option example now introduces the separate requirement to assume similar outstanding instruments; its calculation continues next.
findings: The cap formula defines the senior entitlement, residual participation and ordinary numerator, including zero and negative earnings.
The ordering proof explicitly uses fixed rights and complete nonnegative additive gross earnings effects; it does not reuse fixed ordinary-numerator effects.
The shared-bonus example derives a four-unit error from summing isolated conversion effects. It preserves the unresolved selection rule separately from correct conditional calculations.
